# AI index: ultra log-concavity for increasing families generated by singletons and pairs (v0.2.0-candidate)

Machine-oriented map of claims, evidence and limits. Human readers should start with [README.md](README.md) and the
paper [manuscript.pdf](manuscript.pdf) (source [manuscript.tex](manuscript.tex), which inputs
[supplement/rank_four_section.tex](supplement/rank_four_section.tex)).

## Normalisation

V a ground set with n elements. U an increasing (up-closed) family of subsets of V whose minimal members ("witnesses")
have size at most two: equivalently the dependent sets of a graph with loops allowed. Nonnegative element weights w;
A_k = sum over k-sets S in U of prod_{i in S} w_i. Unweighted case: A_k = d_k, the number of dependent k-sets.
ULC means (A_k / C(n,k)) is log-concave: k(n-k) A_k^2 >= (k+1)(n-k+1) A_{k-1} A_{k+1}, 1 <= k < n.
Source of the conjecture: Xie and Xu, Electron. J. Combin. 33(4) P4.9 (2026), doi:10.37236/13310 (arXiv:2408.09152), Conjecture 4.1.

## Claims and where they are proved

| ID | Claim | Location in the manuscript | Evidence type | Priority status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Weighted ULC for every singleton/pair-generated increasing family and all nonnegative weights; proves Xie-Xu Conjecture 4.1 | Theorem 1.1 (thm:main), Section 4 | proof + exact finite checks | not found earlier in bounded search |
| C2 | Two-colouring theorem: binomially normalised counts of k-sets S with S and V\S both in U are symmetric and unimodal (strengthens Horrocks 2000) | Theorem 1.2 (thm:apu), Section 3 | proof + exact checks | new as stated |
| C3 | Elementary rank comparison and marked-downset comparison (from Katona's intersection-shadow theorem) | Lemmas 2.1-2.2, Section 2 | proof + exhaustive check on downsets of <= 5 elements | new as stated |
| C4 | Boundary identity and critical-element double count | Lemma 3.1, Section 3 | proof + exact checks | new |
| C5 | Closure under conditioning; conditional weighted form; conversion by Kahn-Neiman (JCTA 2011, Theorem 1) | Theorem 4.1 (thm:capu), Section 4 | proof (imported criterion quoted) | new application |
| C6 | ULC of noncover-complex face numbers; variance bound Var(K) <= m(1-m/n) for Bernoulli variables conditioned to hit an edge | Section 5.1, Corollary 5.1 | proof | consequences of C1 |
| C7 | Sharpness: five-element family (counts 0,1,4,10,5,1) gives 96 < 120; two disjoint triples with weights (1,M,M,3,3,3) fail exactly for M >= 44; six elements minimal for uniform-triple counterexample | Section 5.3 | proof + exact checks | new |
| C8 | Weighted strengthening of Xie-Xu Conjecture 4.4 (additive 2-matroids) for rank <= 4 or <= 7 elements; first three inequalities in any rank | Section 6 (supplement/rank_four_section.tex), Theorem 6.1, Lemmas 6.2-6.3, Corollary 6.4 | proof + exhaustive six-element enumeration (corroboration) | new; general conjecture OPEN |
| C9 | Eight-element obstruction to the method at rank five | [supplement/frontier_note.md](supplement/frontier_note.md) | explicit example | limit of method |

## Limits

No human peer review; no formal verification; finite checks are not proofs; bounded priority search. Horrocks (2002)
was read in full: it proves ordinary log-concavity, not ULC; its pair-partition method is credited (supplement/horrocks_2002_comparison.md). Not claimed: real-rootedness, negative correlation, general Conjecture 4.4.
Lorentzian/Mason methods do not apply directly: the natural homogenisation is not M-convex (two disjoint edges).
